fixed: English (UK) now starts. Before, choosing it stopped the game from loading.
changed: A pressed button and a selected item share one look, so you can tell at a glance what you have picked.

new: A search box in Preferences finds an option in any category.
Every window fits the screen at any interface size from 100% to 200%.
The colony window stays in place when you step to the next colony, and you can spy on a colony without the game failing.
The turn banner names the player who is moving, and the monarch's tax-raise message shows the goods that would be boycotted.
A frame-rate meter for the map, under Debug, for checking performance.
The start screen explains what Classic and FreeCol change in the rules, and Classic starts with its four European nations.
BrowserCol has a front page at browsercol.com, with the game at /play/.
fixed: Panning a large map is smooth: the map is drawn in chunks and no longer stalls at the start of a drag.
Sound effects are heard from the first one, and they can overlap.
A ship sailing for Europe is no longer left as your active unit.
Pressing E while typing a save's name no longer opens Europe.
Goods dropped on the docks are sold, and dumping boycotted goods is no longer logged or heard as a sale.
Reports and dialogs fit their content, never grow past the screen, and scroll when they are tall.
Long numbers on goods piles no longer overlap.
A scout meeting a native settlement answers Enter with a request to speak with the chief, not Cancel.
A saved game's address resumes your autosave, and an address naming a save that is gone tells you so.
Escape closes the menu or window on top instead of leaving full screen.
changed: Windows open one at a time, and other units' moves wait until the open one is closed.
Switching the rules on the start screen redraws it in place.
You can export a save as a file from the Open Game window and the start screen.
Nothing is shown under the pointer while you hover or drag, as in FreeCol.
The Colopedia has a fixed size, with its text wrapped.

new: Hovering a rule on the start screen explains it.
changed: Terrain animation on the map is lighter on slow machines.

new: BrowserCol has its own icon, and a wordmark with two globes on the loading screen.
A redesigned window for meeting other nations, treaties and trade.
The Continental Congress shows the father being recruited with the colony's bell bar.
The foreign affairs report is a table, with a column for each nation and a row for each measure.
Trade route stops show the goods they unload, load and keep, by hold.
Price tooltips in the colony window give what Europe would pay and charge, for example Cotton: 3/5 (6).
Buying goods from natives also says what Europe would pay for them.
Music and sound effects are not downloaded while their volume is 0.
Declaring independence and victory use FreeCol's own art.
A ? beside Rules on the start screen explains what each rule set changes.
fixed: Placing a colonist on land that belongs to no colony claims it for the colony.
A ship battle no longer fails in the browser.
Dragging a unit or goods drops it on the place under the pointer.
If saving fails, the game says so. Firefox and Safari players can download a copy of their game.
The Open Game and Save Game windows are wide enough for a save's line.
The Declare Independence windows have titles.
Europe's open panel is no longer reset when the game sends it again.
changed: Tabs have their own look: flat labels with rounded tops and one joined outline.
The map grid is thin and faint when on, and tiles show no seams when it is off.
The default option in a dialog is marked with the focus ring only, and Preferences, Load and the start screen focus their default button.
Colony windows keep a fixed size as you change what is inside.
The Colopedia shows each nation type's abilities and modifiers, the tiles a resource's bonus is for, and units' natives, requirements and production bonuses.
Title music starts with New Game or Continue, and sound keeps playing in the background.
Preferences offers only the graphics quality levels that change the map.
Big empires and animated terrain run faster in Firefox.

new: Music and sound effects have toggles on the start screen. Music is off until you turn it on, and it pauses while the page is hidden.
A wide start screen that fits at 1280×800, with the further options in tabs.
The loading screen shows the build, and warns phones that the game is not made for them.
fixed: A ticked checkbox shows a tick, and a picked radio button shows a dot.
The colonists in Europe's buy menu line up.
The unit order buttons are centred and use FreeCol's icons.
Windows no longer make a sound as they open.
changed: Every clickable thing shows the pointer cursor, and a disabled one does not.
Units ease out of a slide, a diagonal step takes half the time, and the camera waits for a move to finish before it goes on to the next unit.
Animations run as long as FreeCol's own, fast by default.

new: An old browser is told which browsers run the game.
changed: Buttons have FreeCol's bevel instead of flat rounded corners.
Windows open and close with a short scale and fade, and a click on opening.
Hints appear as tooltips that follow the pointer, including on the trade route editor's stops and holds.

new: The first public build: FreeCol's own rules and engine, running in your browser with a new interface that follows FreeCol's layout.
Found colonies, plow, clear forest and build roads, with FreeCol's menu bar, key commands and tile menus.
The colony window: put colonists to work, edit the build queue and buy what is being built, load and unload a ship in the port, and open a colony's tiles.
Europe: buy and sell goods, recruit colonists, sail ships to the New World and back, and pay off a boycott.
Trade routes with an editor, and reports for colonies, labour, trade, religion, requirements and more.
A minimap, a native settlement window, the Colopedia and the Continental Congress.
Saves: autosaves, Save and Open Game, and export and import of FreeCol's .fsg files.
Preferences: FreeCol's own client options, animation speeds, volume and the choice between the FreeCol and FreeCol+ graphics.
Music and sound effects from FreeCol.
